quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: There are oncoming vehicles to your left and parked vehicles to your right. Where should you steer?

options.text: Closer to the oncoming vehicles.
Closer to the parked vehicles.
In the middle, between both groups of vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the middle, between both groups of vehicles.
questions.explanation: Steer in the middle. This gives you the most space from both the oncoming vehicles and the parked vehicles.

questions.question: After a train passes a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Wait for the signal lights to stop flashing.
Check for a second train.
Do both of these things.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do both of these things.
questions.explanation: A second train may be coming on another track. Wait until all gates are raised and all warning lights have stopped flashing before you cross.

questions.question: Before driving, remove snow, frost, and ice from:

options.text: The windshield only.
All windows.
The windshield and passenger window only.

questions.correctAnswerText: All windows.
questions.explanation: You need clear vision through all windows and mirrors. Remove all snow, ice, and frost from every window and mirror before driving.

questions.question: What can help reduce road rage?

options.text: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes.
Talk on your cell phone while driving.
Use your horn often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes.
questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, follow all traffic laws, signs, signals, and road markings. Always signal before you change lanes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield the right-of-way.
No passing zone.
Fewer lanes ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A red and white triangle sign means you must yield the right-of-way to other vehicles.

questions.question: When parking on a hill, you should:

options.text: Have one rear wheel touch the curb.
Use your parking brake and put the car in "park."
Keep your front wheels parallel to the road if there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your parking brake and put the car in "park."
questions.explanation: Always use your parking brake and shift into "park." If there is no curb, turn your wheels away from the road so the car rolls away from traffic if brakes fail. If there is a curb, turn wheels toward it when going downhill, or away from it when going uphill.

questions.question: When is it safe to pass another vehicle?

options.text: At an intersection with no oncoming vehicles.
Only where signs and road markings allow passing.
On a curve with no oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only where signs and road markings allow passing.
questions.explanation: Never pass at intersections, near parking lots, or in alleys. Never pass on curves or hills where you cannot see oncoming traffic. Only pass where signs and markings permit it, and only if you have enough space to pass safely.

questions.question: When bright headlights come toward you at night, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the other car to pass.
Look below the headlights.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at oncoming headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of the road until the other car passes.

questions.question: When may you legally drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?

options.text: Never.
When you can see clearly both directions.
When the warning lights are off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never go around or under a lowered gate. After the gate is raised, only cross the tracks when you can see clearly in both directions and are sure no trains are coming.

questions.question: How do you avoid glare from oncoming headlights?

options.text: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
Focus on the centerline of the road.
Flash your high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at oncoming headlights. Look briefly toward the right side of the road. Then continue looking ahead to track the other vehicle.

questions.question: To turn quickly, where should your hands be on the steering wheel?

options.text: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
Next to each other at the top of the steering wheel.
One at the top and one at the bottom of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Place both hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel. This position helps you turn safely and quickly.

questions.question: Why do large trucks need extra space in front of them?

options.text: So other drivers can merge onto the freeway.
So the truck driver has room to stop.
So other drivers can slow down safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: So the truck driver has room to stop.
questions.explanation: Trucks are larger and take longer to stop than cars at the same speed. Do not pull in front of a truck and then slow down or stop.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in a work zone?

options.text: Speed up to get through the zone quickly.
Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
Keep your normal speed throughout the zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
questions.explanation: Slow down when entering a work zone and be prepared to stop. Follow posted speed limits and stay alert. Workers may be present.

questions.question: As you drive faster, what is important to do?

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Look far ahead of your vehicle.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: As you go faster, your car needs more distance to stop. Look far ahead so you have time to react safely to problems.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you never do?

options.text: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Change lanes suddenly without warning.
Check for other vehicles in the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes suddenly without warning.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors and blind spots before changing lanes. Always use your turn signal so other drivers know what you are doing. Make sure no vehicles are in the space you want to enter.

questions.question: When a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn.
Assume the child controls the bicycle perfectly.
Be ready for anything unexpected.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for anything unexpected.
questions.explanation: Children on bicycles often change direction without warning. Bicycles and young riders are small and hard to see. Always expect them to do something surprising.

questions.question: When a school bus ahead has its red lights flashing on your side of the road, you must:

options.text: Slow down to 10 mph or less.
Stop until the red lights stop flashing.
Change lanes and pass carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the red lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: The flashing red lights and stop arm mean the bus is loading or unloading students. Do not move until the lights stop flashing and the arm goes up. Never pass a school bus that is picking up or dropping off students.

questions.question: If a truck or bus is turning right and you also need to turn right, you should:

options.text: Turn quickly before the truck or bus.
Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning.
Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning.
questions.explanation: Do not try to fit your car between a turning truck or bus and the curb. This can cause a serious crash. Wait until the truck or bus has finished turning before you turn.

questions.question: What headlights should you use in rain or fog?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain, snow, or fog. High beams reflect off water and back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: When turning left, drivers must yield to:

options.text: Oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right.
Passing cars.
No one in particular.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right.
questions.explanation: Drivers turning left must yield to all vehicles coming toward them. This includes bicycles and motorcycles.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires slide on water instead of the road. How can you prevent hydroplaning in rain?

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when it rains to reduce hydroplaning risk. Driving too fast can make your tires slide on water and lose grip on the road. This makes your vehicle hard to control.

questions.question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is true?

options.text: If you can walk in a straight line after drinking, it is safe to drive.
If you are below the legal alcohol limit, your driving is not impaired.
Alcohol affects your judgment, which you need to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol affects your judgment, which you need to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol harms your judgment. You need good judgment to react to what you see or hear on the road. Even a small amount of alcohol can hurt your driving ability, even if you are below the legal limit.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down and drive carefully through.
Stop completely, check traffic, and go when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, check traffic, and go when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a full stop, give way to other traffic and pedestrians, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: Alcohol in any amount is:

options.text: A stimulant.
A depressant.
Neither of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is always a depressant. It slows your nerve impulses and body functions. It reduces inhibitions and hurts your ability to focus and stay alert.

questions.question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, you should:

options.text: Use low beam headlights.
Use high beam headlights until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.
Use high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use high beams only in rural areas when no other cars are near. Switch to low beams when driving closely behind another vehicle.

questions.question: Your chest should be ____ from the center of the steering wheel.

options.text: 10 to 12 inches
5 inches
20 inches

questions.correctAnswerText: 10 to 12 inches
questions.explanation: Adjust your seat before driving so you can see 12 to 15 feet ahead on the road. Your chest should be 10 to 12 inches from the steering wheel center. Your shoulders should be at or above the top of the steering wheel.

questions.question: Hard braking on ice and snow often:

options.text: Helps you stop faster.
Locks the front wheels, causing loss of steering control.
Keeps the brakes from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Locks the front wheels, causing loss of steering control.
questions.explanation: Hard braking on snow and ice can lock the front wheels, making you lose control of steering. Avoid hard braking by driving at a safe speed for the conditions.

questions.question: Why should drivers give children on bikes extra space?

options.text: They do not have the same quick reflexes as adults.
They are smaller and harder to see than adults.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Children are often unpredictable and hard to see. Watch carefully for children near schools, bus stops, playgrounds, parks, and ice cream trucks. Be aware that children on bikes may suddenly come onto the road.

questions.question: When driving behind a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.
Drive more slowly.
Keep a larger following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a larger following distance.
questions.explanation: Stay at least 3 to 4 seconds behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles stop quickly, and following too closely is dangerous. You need extra space in case the rider falls. Falls are more likely on wet roads, ice, gravel, and metal surfaces like bridges and railroad tracks.

questions.question: If your vehicle's rear is skidding to the left, you should:

options.text: Not turn your steering wheel.
Turn your steering wheel to the left.
Turn your steering wheel to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel to the left.
questions.explanation: If you skid on a wet or icy road, take your foot off the gas, avoid braking, and turn your wheel in the direction of the skid. If your vehicle has anti-lock brakes, press the brake pedal firmly and steer straight.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on your high beam headlights.
Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Speed up to avoid an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use low beam lights. If fog is too thick to see, pull off the road and wait for it to clear.

questions.question: Where should children age 12 and under sit in a vehicle with airbags?

options.text: The front seat.
The back seat.
The bed of a pick-up truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back seat.
questions.explanation: Airbags can be dangerous for children. All children age 12 and under should sit in the back seat.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for bicycles.
Bicycles not allowed.
Bicycle repair shop ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for bicycles.
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black markings are warning signs. They alert drivers to watch for bicycles, animals, and pedestrians.

questions.question: When should you use turn signals when parking next to a curb?

options.text: Only when pulling away from the curb.
Only when pulling next to the curb.
Both when pulling next to and away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both when pulling next to and away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Always signal when pulling next to a curb or away from a curb.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on your left.
The driver who arrived first.
The driver across from you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrived first.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, vehicles go in the order they arrive. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the one on the right goes first.

questions.question: When a vehicle enters the interstate from a ramp ahead of you, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to pass them.
Change lanes to let them merge safely.
Ignore them because you have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to let them merge safely.
questions.explanation: Make room for vehicles entering the interstate. Change lanes when possible to let them merge safely.

questions.question: How do you know where traffic is behind you?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror often.
Turn and look out your back window.
Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your rearview mirror often.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror frequently to see traffic behind you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A divided highway is ending.
A divided highway is starting.
The road ahead will be slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: A divided highway is starting.
questions.explanation: This sign means a divided highway is starting. Stay to the right of the median.

questions.question: What does a pennant-shaped sign mean?

options.text: No passing zone.
Right turn allowed on red.
Yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone.
questions.explanation: A pennant-shaped sign marks the start of a no passing zone.

questions.question: When should you stop waiting behind a school bus with flashing red lights?

options.text: When all students are off the bus.
When the stop arm is pulled back.
When the stop arm is pulled back and the bus starts moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the stop arm is pulled back and the bus starts moving.
questions.explanation: Stay stopped behind a school bus with flashing red lights until the lights turn off, the stop arm is pulled back, and the bus starts moving.
